newsitem.title: FINLAND: HARD TO JOIN BROAD PAY DEAL - PAPER BOSS LAHTEENMAKI.
newsitem.headline: HARD TO JOIN BROAD PAY DEAL - PAPER BOSS LAHTEENMAKI.

text.p: For the Finnish Paper Workers' Union, joining a broad pay deal for 1998 looks difficult, if not impossible, union chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki said on Monday.
"At the moment it seems that it will be difficult, if not impossible, for the paper workers' union to join a possible new comprehensive incomes settlement," Lahteenmaki told a union congress meeting.
He said the union wanted pay hikes in 1998 to reflect productivity increases, and that workers needed to settle sectors-specific problems with employers in next autumn's pay talks.
"Of course our target is a real earnings development based on the productivity development of labour in the sector," he said.
"The Paper Workers' Union is not out for pay hikes with any mentality of distraint, but we want and need to settle our sector-specific problems," he added.

Lahteenmaki said the problems for the union were the industry's use of non-paper workers -- which has been shelved and where a "sustainable and permanenent" solution is necessary -- and working hours arrangements.
"The union has wished to talk about ... a controlled lowering of the threshold between production and maintenance as a way to reduce the use of non-paper worker labour," he added.
